title: What do the Olympic ring colours mean?

sources.name: International Olympic Committee — What is the meaning of the Olympic rings?

practice: Ready for another sporting question? Try the Sports Quiz.

sections.html:
The five Olympic rings represent the union of five continents and athletes meeting from around the world. No individual ring colour is officially assigned to a continent.

The International Olympic Committee explains the design as a whole. A neat colour-coded map may be memorable, but that does not make it the official explanation.
sections.title: Do the colours stand for different continents?

sections.html:
Pierre de Coubertin created the rings in 1913. The IOC explains that the five colours, together with the white background, represented the colours found in national flags at the time.

White is easy to overlook because it sits behind the rings. Quietly doing the background work still counts.
sections.title: Why blue, yellow, black, green and red?

sections.html:
If someone asks which continent the blue ring represents, there is no official individual assignment to give. Think of the linked design as a whole.
